title: Clitoria ternatea — Plants of the World Online
scope: Accepted species identity, family Fabaceae, taxonomy and native-range context; not cultivar-specific cultivation

title: Butterfly Pea (Clitoria ternatea) — Plant Toolbox
scope: Species-level outdoor habit, full-sun and soil guidance, temperate annual use, propagation strategy and possible pest issues; not hydroponics

title: Butterfly Pea — Gardening Solutions
scope: Outdoor vine support, seed timing, edible parts, flower/color use and Florida seasonal context; not a germination-temperature or indoor hydroponics source

title: Moringa oleifera — Plants of the World Online
scope: Accepted species identity, family Moringaceae, synonyms, native range and broad ecological context; not cultivar-specific horticulture

publisher: University of California Agriculture and Natural Resources Cooperative Extension
title: Moringa oleifera (Miracle tree) — Central Sierra Agriculture
scope: Regional Central California cultivation, direct sow/nursery starts, 7–14 day germination report, cold sensitivity, pruning/leaf-versus-pod production, and a reported frost-season cutback/covering practice; documents food uses of fresh/cooked leaves, dried/powdered leaves and pods but not medical efficacy, food-processing safety or a universal climate/hydroponic recommendation

title: Lippia origanoides — Plants of the World Online
scope: Accepted species name, synonyms including Lippia graveolens, family Verbenaceae, native range, shrub habit and broad recorded food use; not a home cultivation guide

title: Vegetative propagation and early growth of Lippia origanoides (alecrim-de-tabuleiro)
scope: Species-specific Brazilian experiment on apical-cutting propagation of Lippia origanoides; supports the tested cutting route and relative early-growth result for a 1:1 commercial-substrate/expanded-vermiculite mix. Does not establish a general home success rate, seed protocol, or universal cultivation prescription.

publisher: African Journal of Plant Science; Universidade Estadual de Santa Cruz research team
title: Different levels of irradiance and plant regulators modify the leaf structure and essential oil production of Lippia origanoides H.B.K (Verbenaceae)
scope: Species-specific subtropical Bahia pot experiment: plants grown in soil:sand 4:1 under full sun or reduced-irradiance treatments, with and without a biostimulant. Supports the trial context and higher leaf essential-oil content under full sun in that experiment only; not a universal home light, water, or fertilizer recommendation.

publisher: Instituto Nacional de Investigaciones Forestales, Agrícolas y Pecuarias (INIFAP), Mexico
title: Domesticación del orégano para zonas semidesérticas de Coahuila
scope: Mexican oregano reported as Lippia graveolens, cross-referenced to Lippia origanoides through the Kew synonym record. Describes a regional arid-Coahuila commercial drip-irrigation production context, soil/water conditions, a 120-day cycle and two foliage cuts per year; not home-container targets, cultivar-specific performance or a universal schedule.

publisher: Revista Chapingo Serie Ciencias Forestales y del Ambiente; INIFAP CENID-RASPA and Universidad Autónoma Chapingo
title: Influence of irrigation frequency on oregano (Lippia graveolens HKB) growth
scope: Field experiment in arid Durango on Lippia graveolens, a synonym of Lippia origanoides in Kew. Compares post-transplant irrigation intervals and reports water-use-efficiency and later biomass tradeoffs; not a watering schedule for home pots, indoor systems or hydroponics.

publisher: UC Sustainable Agriculture Research and Education Program; UC Cooperative Extension Fresno & Tulare Counties
title: A Guide to Drying Moringa
scope: California small-farm guide to washing, drying and storing Moringa oleifera leaves. Reports tested indoor air-drying and dehydrator conditions and food-handling practices; times vary with environment and equipment and are not a guaranteed household shelf life or food-safety substitute.
